M Admit.
of Considered I.A.No.21747/2017, an application for stay.
Petitioner has been convicted for misbranding under the rt provisions of Food Safety Act and Rule 3.1.2(1) of the Food Safety ou and Standards Rules, 2011 for allegedly using photographs of C vegetables on the packet of salt for sale.
h In the case of M/s Parakh Foods Ltd. Vs. State of A.P. in ig criminal Appeal No.559/2008 decided on 27.3.2008, the Apex Court H has held that until the pictures of vegetables on the label of edible oils and fats exaggerates the quality of the product, it would not fall with the mischief of Rule 37D.
The vegetable pictures on the label of Soyabean oil do not indicate that the quality of Soyabean Oil is super- refined, extra-refined, micro-refined, double-refined, ultra-refined, anti-cholesterol,
cholesterol fighter, soothing to heart, cholesterol friendly, saturated fat free etc, nor it indicates the exaggeration of the quality of the product to come within the meaning of PFA Rules.
